Topsoil respreading is based on average premining topsoil depths since some areas are devoid of suitable topsoil material. Where shortages occur stockpiles are utilized. There is sufficient topsoil within Tracts II and III to negate the usage of non-topsoil material (David W. Simpson, Westmoreland Resources, personal comm.). Replaced topsoils are seeded with recommended plant species at the first opportunity. Rapid reestablishment of vegetation will mitigate the loss of topsoil through wind and water erosion. Direct topsoiling will mitigate adverse effects of stockpiling on soil organisms.
Overburden studies are completed prior to mining so that strata with phytotoxic or other undesirable characteristics are identified.

Mixing of strata during excavation and recontouring is expected to dilute undesirable intervals in most cases. Overburden and interburden are mixed to some extent because in excavating to the Robinson seam, a large amount of overburden is rehandled in the process. If situations arise where undesirable overburden characteristics cannot be mitigated by mixing, the mining sequence will be modified to bury toxic strata below the plant rooting zone where possible. Regraded spoils are sampled prior to topsoiling and if problems are identified, fill is hauled in to provide an adequate rooting zone. Burial depths in such situations are regulated by the Montana Department of State Lands, and current regulations require eight feet of non-toxic material.
